subject.title: Bug: OpenClaw 2026.4.9 exposes agent internal thinking (English) to user

question: Should maintainers approve a narrow core/shared sanitizer fix for attribute-bearing reasoning tags on the embedded streaming path now, or fold this into a broader channel-leak policy effort?
rationale: The source fix shape is narrow, but the item is security-sensitive, affects external chat recipients, and is already labeled for no-new-fix-pr and security review.

options.title: Approve narrow sanitizer fix
options.body: Update the embedded streaming scanner to match the shared reasoning-tag grammar and require focused tests for attributes, namespaces, chunk boundaries, code spans, and explicit reasoning stream behavior.

options.title: Fold into broader leak policy
options.body: Keep this issue open as a dependency of the broader channel-leak work if maintainers want one coordinated delivery-policy change instead of a standalone sanitizer repair.

options.title: Defer pending live proof
options.body: Ask for a fresh WeChat/weixin proof before changing core, accepting that current source still shows a mismatch in the shipped scanner.

recommendation.title: Approve narrow sanitizer fix
recommendation.body: Update the embedded streaming scanner to match the shared reasoning-tag grammar and require focused tests for attributes, namespaces, chunk boundaries, code spans, and explicit reasoning stream behavior.
